chunks.title: CLO Tips Workshop - Custom OBJ Outlines
chunks.content: ## CLO Custom OBJ Outlines Workflow Overview This section explains the process of creating and exporting custom OBJ outlines (OPT files) in CLO software, focusing on model placement, export settings, and importing outlines for garment parts. Key terms include OPT export, name line, UV coordinates, and scale adjustment. ### Model Preparation and OPT Export Begin by building your model in CLO using simple template objects, such as three small cubes. Arrange the model properly—center it and place it on the floor grid in the 3D window. To verify correct placement, ensure the floor grid is visible and identify the X-axis direction, which the name line will follow repeatedly. Switch to the 5-angle view (shortcut key: 5) for a clear perspective where the X-axis appears horizontal. This alignment is crucial because the name line will repeat along the X-axis, which corresponds to the blue, red, and yellow axes in the 3D window. To export the model: 1. Go to the menu bar, select **Export > OPT**. 2. Choose a save location (e.g., desktop) and remember the file name. 3. In the export OPT window: - Set the target to **Single** (thick one). - Check **Unified UV Coordinates**. - Ignore unnecessary options like "發現 picture". - Scroll down and choose to save as a compressed package. 4. Click **OK** to export. After export, unzip the compressed package to access the OPT file. ### Importing and Configuring OPT Name Lines Open the garment file in CLO (e.g., a skirt model). To complete garment features such as straps: - Switch to the thick texture surface. - Disable display of inner and basic lines for clarity. - Zoom in on the area to add the name line (e.g., shoulder strap). Create a new name line by clicking **Add**. The OPT name line window appears with settings on the left and a preview pane on the right (initially empty). Click **Browse** to locate and open the previously exported OPT file. The preview will show the outline with its length and width corresponding to the OPT file dimensions. ### Adjusting Scale, Rotation, and Line Settings - **Scale** controls the distance between repeated OPT units along the name line. - The exported three small objects count as one unit. - Modifying scale to 10mm sets a 10mm gap between repeated groups. - Reset scale to 0 for no spacing. Rotation settings allow the OPT to rotate around the X, Y, and Z axes if needed, but typically these are preset and do not require adjustment on import. ### Adding Lines and UV Images - Use the free line tool to add lines to the board. - Newly added lines appear gray because they don't yet have UV images applied. - Select the added lines in the object window. - Click **Browse** behind the text field to add corresponding UV images. Repeat this process for all relevant garment parts, such as shoulder boards.
